subject: Quant
topic: Time and work III — mixed tiers
description: Time-and-work problems with efficiency ratios, alternate days, leaving partway

questions.stem: A and B together can finish a job in 12 days. A alone takes 20 days. B alone will take how many days?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 per day. A's rate = 1/20. B's rate = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 → B alone takes 30 days. Distractor 24 → if you mistakenly compute 1/12 + 1/20 instead of subtracting. Distractor 36 → 12 × 3.
questions.subject: Quant
questions.topic: Time and work III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: A is 50% more efficient than B. If B alone can finish a piece of work in 30 days, A alone will finish it in:

options.option_text: 20 days to finish the work alone
25 days to finish the work alone
18 days to finish the work alone

questions.explanation: Efficiency ratio A : B = 1.5 : 1 = 3 : 2. Time ratio is the INVERSE = 2 : 3. If B = 30 days → A = 30 × (2/3) = 20 days. Distractor 15 → if you mistakenly halve. Distractor 25 → arbitrary. Distractor 18 → 30 × 0.6.

questions.stem: A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B in 10 days. They work on alternate days, A starting first. The work will be completed in:
questions.explanation: LCM(15, 10) = 30 units of work. A = 2 units/day, B = 3 units/day. In 2 days (one A-day + one B-day) they do 5 units. After 5 such pairs (10 days): 25 units done; 5 units left. Day 11 (A's turn): A does 2 → 27 done, 3 left. Day 12 (B's turn): B does 3 → done. Total 12 days.

questions.stem: A and B together can do a job in 8 days. B and C together can do it in 12 days. A and C together can do it in 16 days. How long will all three take working together?
questions.explanation: (A+B) + (B+C) + (A+C) = 1/8 + 1/12 + 1/16 = 6/48 + 4/48 + 3/48 = 13/48. This equals 2(A+B+C). So (A+B+C) = 13/96 per day → time = 96/13 ≈ 7.38 days. Distractor 6.4 → forgot to halve. Distractor 9.6 → 96/10. Distractor 5.8 → arbitrary.

questions.stem: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. After 6 days, 4 men leave. The remaining men will take how many more days?
questions.explanation: Total man-days = 12 × 18 = 216. Done in first 6 days = 12 × 6 = 72 → 144 left. After 4 leave, 8 men remain. Days needed = 144 / 8 = 18 days. Distractor 16 → 144/9. Distractor 12 → 144/12 (forgot 4 left). Distractor 24 → 144/6.

questions.stem: A can do a work in 24 days. He works for 4 days, then B alone finishes the remaining work in 15 days. B alone could do the whole work in:

options.option_text: 20 days alone to do whole job
18 days alone to do whole job
16 days alone to do whole job
22 days alone to do whole job

questions.explanation: A in 4 days does 4/24 = 1/6 of work. Remaining = 5/6. B does 5/6 in 15 days → B's whole-work time = 15 × (6/5) = 18 days. Distractor 20 → 15 × (4/3). Distractor 16 → arbitrary. Distractor 22 → arbitrary.

questions.stem: A is twice as good as B. Together they finish a work in 18 days. A alone will finish it in:
questions.explanation: Efficiency A : B = 2 : 1. Combined rate = 1/18 → 3 parts = 1/18 → 1 part = 1/54. A's rate = 2 parts = 2/54 = 1/27 → A alone = 27 days. Quick check: B = 54 days; 1/27 + 1/54 = 2/54 + 1/54 = 3/54 = 1/18. ✓
